**How to falsify it:** If genetic analysis reveals that the causal variants for rhizomelic chondrodysplasia punctata type 1 do not impact peroxisomal import pathways, or if the accumulation of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaric acid is found to be unrelated to HMGCL deficiency in patients with 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaric aciduria, this hypothesis would be falsified. _(variant: Absence of pathogenic variants in PEX7 and HMGCL in large control populations like gnomAD would strengthen the hypothesis, while presence of common pathogenic variants would weaken it.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this mechanistic link could inform therapeutic strategies. For instance, therapies aimed at improving peroxisomal function or mitigating the downstream effects of 3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaric acid accumulation might benefit patients with either condition, particularly those presenting with overlapping severe phenotypes. This could include metabolic interventions or gene therapy approaches targeting the respective causal genes.
